summary: Lycoming County, PA steel tower built 1921 on Holmes Hill, moved in 1938 and renamed Sprout Point, removed 1985; a trail guide describes the site, not any standing structure.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1985 per the register; the trail guide does not say whether any structure remains

access.note: State forest land reached by an ungraded dirt road and a short hike, per a trail guide; no agency page for the site was found

visit.trail_note: The road ends at the old tower site. The tower itself cannot be reached by vehicle; an easy hike up the trail reaches the location, per the trail guide.

corrections.why: The state spells the forest Tiadaghton; Tiadachton is a variant spelling used on the Forest Lookouts page. Which forest the site lies in is still disputed (see notes).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1938 for the Sprout Point tower; the October 1937 newspaper already describes it as being erected. The story reads these as one project finished in 1938.
The Forest Lookouts page spells the forest Tiadachton, which is a variant of the state's Tiadaghton. This explains the spelling only.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: the Forest Lookouts page says Tiadachton State Forest, while the trail guide says Sprout Point Road is in Loyalsock State Forest. A human should decide which forest the record should name. The register's 1938 build date and the 1937 newspaper's erection date are treated as one project. Whether any structure survives is unknown; the trail guide does not say. An urbex listing in search results says the tower was removed, but that page returned HTTP 403 and is not used. Record elevation 689.8 m matches the register's 2,263 ft (690 m). The 1922 towerman was at the Holmes Hill tower before it was moved; the register treats that steel tower as the one that became Sprout Point.
